name: Boerhavia

curation_status.status: morphology-first lesson expanded; mature fruit macros and arrows pending

look_here_first: Find a mature anthocarp first. Check for stalked glands versus glabrous surface, then the shape of its five ribs and grooves. Next compare fruit apex, perianth and stamens; do not rely on flower color or leaf width.
shared_genus_traits: Tiny clustered flowers with a single petaloid perianth whorl (no separate corolla).
One-seeded fruit enclosed by the persistent basal perianth (anthocarp), typically prominently five-ribbed.
Leaf and flower color variation makes mature fruit characters especially important.

species_comparison_matrix.erecta: Diffuse branching clusters, fruit apex truncate/low-conic

quick_comparison_steps: Collect mature fruits from several branches; use a hand lens and millimeter scale.
Separate densely glandular B. coccinea from glabrous B. erecta/B. linearifolia.
Among glabrous fruits, inspect rib shape, grooves, and fruit apex.
Photograph flower clusters, perianth, stamens and full plant as supporting evidence.
overlap_and_cautions: B. diffusa and the B. intermedia / B. triquetra var. intermedia complex need separate keyed comparison before firm IDs.
All three currently have UNRESOLVED project target-zone range; Texas state-level native is not the project PASS threshold.
Current one-photo set shows flower/habit but not definitive mature fruit macros.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched scale-bearing mature anthocarp macro for each species
B. coccinea vs B. diffusa stalked-glandular fruit surface
B. erecta vs intermedia cluster and pedicel insertion
B. linearifolia perianth and exserted stamens
sources: Flora of North America Boerhavia treatment
Kew Plants of the World Online accepted taxa

learning_sequence.approach: See it → Spot it → Name it → Compare it → Remember it
look_here_first: Find several fully mature anthocarps (persistent perianth bases surrounding the fruit), not just flowers.
At 10–20× magnification, check whether the anthocarp is densely stalked-glandular or smooth.
On smooth anthocarps compare the five rib edges, grooves and fruit apex; photograph with a millimeter scale.
Check flower perianth, exserted stamens, habit and leaf distribution only as supporting clues.
learning_sequence.shared_morphology: Boerhavia in this learner has tiny clustered flowers with a single petaloid perianth whorl (not separate petals and sepals); the persistent perianth base encloses a one-seeded fruit as a five-ribbed anthocarp. Leaf width, habit and flower color are variable, so mature anthocarp anatomy is the practical genus/species entry point.

plain_language_glossary.meaning: Fruit-like unit formed when the persistent base of the flower's perianth encloses the seed-bearing fruit.
Tiny sticky-looking gland perched on a short hairlike stalk on the fruit surface.
Raised longitudinal ridge / groove between ridges on a mature anthocarp.

overlap_cautions: Measured fruit length overlaps heavily: coccinea 2.6–4 mm, erecta 2.7–4 mm, linearifolia 2.5–3.5 mm. Size alone cannot separate them.
Flower color and narrow leaves vary and are not reliable tie-breakers.
Use several mature fruits from the same plant, with a scale, because immature and damaged anthocarps obscure glands, ribs and apex.
B. diffusa can also have glandular anthocarps; gland presence alone does not prove B. coccinea.
Historical B. intermedia / B. triquetra var. intermedia concepts complicate B. erecta-like material; send doubtful records to taxonomy review rather than force an ID.

comparison_cards.title: Stalked-glandular versus smooth fruit
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Inspect the surface of multiple mature anthocarps under magnification.
comparison_cards.separates: B. coccinea typically densely stalked-glandular; the other two glabrous. Do not use flower color.
comparison_cards.overlap: B. diffusa can also be glandular; confirm further keyed characters.
comparison_cards.photo_role: same-scale side views of mature anthocarps with clear glands and scale

comparison_cards.title: Two smooth-fruited spiderlings
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare five fruit ribs and apex; use perianth and stamens as supporting characters.
comparison_cards.separates: B. erecta acute ribs and truncate/low-conic apex; B. linearifolia broadly rounded ribs, smooth grooves, perianth 4–7 mm and usually five exserted stamens.
comparison_cards.overlap: Fruit lengths overlap and immature rib edges are misleading; do not decide from leaf width alone.
comparison_cards.photo_role: matched glabrous anthocarp end/side views and perianth side views

comparison_cards.title: Common look-alikes beyond the three cards
comparison_cards.look_here_first: For coccinea-like fruit compare B. diffusa; for erecta-like fruit check historical intermedia/triquetra complex.
comparison_cards.separates: Use mature anthocarp surface, ribs, apex and inflorescence arrangement together.
comparison_cards.overlap: Not all look-alike names are installed or taxonomically settled in this learner.
comparison_cards.photo_role: taxonomically verified comparison anthocarps from look-alike taxa

anatomy_lessons.title: 1 · Anthocarp: the fruit is wrapped in flower tissue
anatomy_lessons.structure: persistent basal perianth and one-seeded fruit
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: What looks like a small seed or fruit is surrounded by the surviving base of the flower.
anatomy_lessons.look_for: Mature ribbed anthocarp attached to its stalk; distinguish from a bud.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: This is the correct structure for the genus-level field key.

anatomy_lessons.title: 2 · Glands on mature fruit
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: Look for little stalks with glandular tips, not just general hairiness.
anatomy_lessons.look_for: Densely stalked-glandular coccinea compared with glabrous erecta/linearifolia; compare diffusa separately.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Best first split of the installed three-species group.

anatomy_lessons.title: 3 · Five ribs, grooves and fruit tip
anatomy_lessons.structure: longitudinal ribs, sulci and anthocarp apex
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: Look at whether ridges are sharp or round and how the fruit ends.
anatomy_lessons.look_for: Acute ribs and low-conic/truncate tip in erecta versus broadly rounded ribs and smooth grooves in linearifolia.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Best second split after checking glands; fruit lengths overlap.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: matched side and tip views of fully mature glabrous fruits with ruler

anatomy_lessons.title: 4 · Petaloid perianth and stamens
anatomy_lessons.structure: single perianth whorl and projecting stamens
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: The colored flower part is one perianth whorl; it is not a separate true corolla.
anatomy_lessons.look_for: Flower tube and exserted stamens; linearifolia commonly has five exserted stamens.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Teaches family recognition and provides supporting evidence when fruit is absent.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: flower side-view with stamens in focus; fruit comparison still required
